primary.poolable_reason: TWO TRIALS THAT SHARE NEITHER A COMPARATOR NOR AN OUTCOME. Registrations read from ClinicalTrials.gov on 2026-08-18. NCT03537508 compares the MenACYW conjugate vaccine against MENVEO; NCT03691610 compares it against different meningococcal polysaccharide preparations across four groups. DIFFERENT COMPARATOR VACCINES MEAN DIFFERENT QUESTIONS -- the same shape that closed the azilsartan topic in cardiology. The outcome compounds it: both register PERCENTAGE SERORESPONSE, but seroresponse is reported SEPARATELY FOR EACH OF FOUR SEROGROUPS (A, C, Y, W), so there is no single quantity to pool, and the two trials stratify by different age bands -- NCT03537508 from 42 days, NCT03691610 from 6 months, with group structures that do not correspond. AUTHORITY: MECIR Box 10.10.a C62 -- 'Undertake (or display) a meta-analysis only if participants, interventions, comparisons and outcomes are judged to be sufficiently similar to ensure an answer that is clinically meaningful.'

primary.what_this_verdict_does_not_establish: NOT that any trial here is poor -- each is registered and reports its own primary. NOT that the drug is ineffective; both lenacapavir trials in fact report striking results on their own terms. NOT that no poolable question exists in this area: only that the question this page's title asks cannot be answered by pooling the trials this page carries. THE CRITICISM IS OF THE POOLING AND OF NOTHING ELSE. The registry is a live document and this reads its contents on 2026-08-18; a later amendment could change it.
primary.what_a_poolable_version_would_need: A shared comparator vaccine, a single named serogroup, and corresponding age strata. Each is available in principle; none is available across THESE two registrations.
primary.an_immunogenicity_caveat_worth_recording: Seroresponse percentage is a surrogate. Even a well-formed pool of it would not estimate protection against meningococcal disease, and a page titled for healthy volunteers should not be read as reporting one.
primary.poolable_DEPRECATED_note: `poolable` MEANT ONLY 'the source page pooled these trials'. It was never a judgement that the pool was sound, and the renderer read it as permission to assert 'pooled on the X scale'. RENAMED to source_page_pooled, which is what it says. `poolable` is retained so nothing breaks, and it is DEPRECATED: read source_page_pooled for what the source did, and estimand_established for whether the pool is defensible. A PAGE SHOULD DISPLAY A POOLED ESTIMATE BECAUSE ITS ESTIMAND WAS ESTABLISHED, NOT BECAUSE SOMEONE ONCE POOLED IT.
primary.estimand_established_means: TRUE only where every contributing trial has been READ and shown to measure the same quantity, or the same construct with a variance stated. FALSE where that was checked and failed. NULL where it was never checked -- AN ABSENT ASSERTION AND A NEGATIVE ONE ARE DIFFERENT STATES and null is not a pass.
primary.estimand_established_does_not_cover_the_: READ THIS BESIDE `estimand_established`. That flag records that every contributing trial measures the SAME QUANTITY. It records NOTHING about what that quantity was measured AGAINST -- whether the comparators are of one kind, whether each comparison was randomised, whether it was concurrent. On attr-pn-review the flag is TRUE and correct while the pool combines patisiran against its own saline placebo, vutrisiran against PATISIRAN, and eplontersen against the placebo cohort of a DIFFERENT TRIAL. The two questions were never separated. Named as P48 in PAGE-STANDARD.md v1.21.0 and swept by scripts/audit_mixed_contrast_pools.py.

outcomes.measure_note: THE GENERATOR'S OWN IDIOM FOR ABSENCE, not a borrowed measure. Its code renders "not stated" rather than a zero where an object is silent, with the comment "a zero is a claim" -- so a marker is the established convention here. This topic publishes no estimate and never computed one, so there is no measure it was expressed in. Sibling verdict-only objects such as acs-antiplatelet-review DO carry a real measure because their estimate was WITHDRAWN and the withdrawn value had one: a different case. A null broke the generator's escape function; an inherited "OR" would have been a defaulted-field lie on a published page.
